title: No parameter-independent positive prime-index channel realizes strict eta contraction
question: Can the Fisher-natural flow eta -> c eta be realized by one fixed stochastic channel on prime powers, thereby linking the prime feature law to an arithmetic splice operation?

verdict.conclusion: No parameter-independent Markov kernel on prime powers can map every p_a in an open parameter interval to p_(2+c(a-2)) for any 0<c<1. Analyticity extends such an identity to all real a>1; concentration at the first support point forces the kernel to fix n=2, while the contracted target requires more n=3 mass than the input has outside n=2. This blocks a natural positive-channel bridge for the feature-family flow, but does not rule out a nonlinear same-xi identity or an operator specified only on actual zeros.

family.support: prime powers n with Lambda(n)>0, ordered 2<3<4<...
family.parameterRelation: a=2+2eta; eta -> c eta is a -> a_c=2+c(a-2)

proof.assumption: A fixed column-stochastic kernel K(r|n)>=0 satisfies sum_n K(r|n)p_a(n)=p_(a_c)(r) for every a in a nonempty open subinterval of (1,3).
proof.analyticContinuation: For each output r, F_r(z)=sum_n K(r|n)Lambda(n)n^(-z) is holomorphic on Re(z)>1. After cross multiplication by M(z)M(a_c), the assumed identity is holomorphic on Re(z)>1 and hence holds throughout that half-plane.
proof.firstSupportPoint: As real a->infinity, p_a converges in total variation to delta_2 and p_(a_c) also converges to delta_2. Therefore K delta_2=delta_2, so K(3|2)=0.
proof.contradiction: The ratio of required target mass to available non-2 input mass is asymptotic to (2/3)^(a_c-a)=(3/2)^((1-c)(a-2)), which tends to infinity for 0<c<1. This contradicts stochasticity.
proof.scope: The identity on an open interval is essential for analytic continuation. The theorem does not forbid an eta-dependent resampling rule, a signed/non-Markov operator, or a rule defined only on a discrete unknown set of actual zero displacements.

relationToOtherExactBridges.primePairSpliceAudit: The (101,101) self-pair vanishes in centered Fisher curvature; the current no-go rules out a single stochastic channel as the missing same-xi coupling.
relationToOtherExactBridges.criticalEnergy: The all-scale critical Chebyshev-energy bound still implies RH by Mellin holomorphy, but remains RH-equivalent and unproved.
relationToOtherExactBridges.primeAnchor: The positive defect D_2 is an exact prime-to-horizontal-zero identity; proving D_2=0 remains RH-equivalent.
relationToOtherExactBridges.remainingTarget: Find a nonlinear, same-xi arithmetic identity/conservation law that couples the actual completed zero divisor to the fixed prime ledger; this channel route cannot supply it.

status: A candidate positive-channel bridge is ruled out exactly. No new same-xi identity, zero-free strip or RH proof is obtained.
